fundamental.headline: Strong business, but expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 34% over the last year, it keeps 36 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, its debt is easily covered by earnings.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying more than usual: its price vs sales is higher than 85% of the last 5 years. Compared with similar companies, adjusted for growth, it's priced about in line.
drivers: Sales growth is speeding up compared with six months ago.
Profit margins are widening: it keeps more of each sale than a year ago.
news: No major company news in the last two weeks.
fundamental.take: Great business, but you're paying up for it: fine to own, better to add slowly or wait for a pullback. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 15% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 34% last year; 3%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 11% (3 years ago 9%, about the same) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $11 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 12% (3 years ago 10%).

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 54% vs quarterly sales up 40% (days to collect 49 → 54). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 3%/yr over 3 years and 16%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 36% vs a 5-year range of 19–36% (median 26%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $5.2B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($3.1B buybacks + $2.0B dividends) = 2.9% of the company's market value. Share count down 1.6% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $16.50, up 10% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 4 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $12.88, up 4% in 90 days; 3 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +68% vs a year ago · $8.46 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 68% vs sales 40%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running by about 4%, yet the stock fell after 4 of them: beats are already expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 40% from a year ago and speeding up (from 30% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $36 of operating profit, up from $25 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: It turned 119% of its reported profit into spare cash: the profits are real money, not just accounting.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 43× last year's profit (lower than 62% of the last 5 years); only 22× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Nov 24; analysts expect EPS of $3.88, up 72% from a year ago. It usually moves about 4% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 10% in 90 days (4 raised, 0 cut lately): forecasts are edging up.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
